doc.title: Allan Vaché interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000

title: Sibling rivalry with brother and the Mrs. Vache's Boys record
summary: Rivalry and occasional tension with his brother; their Nagel-Heyer album was well reviewed.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah. Interesting. Did you and your brother have any kind of sibling rivalry going with the music?

Oh yes and no. We still have a little bit. But as we get older it kind of wanes in the noonday sun, as O. Henry said. We’ve learned to live with each other a little bit. But my brother has a tendency to be a little bit high strung. His temper can sometimes get the best of him. We’ve had our hassles over the years but basically we still get along pretty well. And we just did a record for this label that I record on, Nagel-Heyer Records, and this is “Mrs. Vache’s Boys,” that’s been selling very well, it just got voted number two in Jazz Journal International for 1999. So we’re both pretty proud of it.
You don’t call each other up every week and say so how many gigs did you have this week?

No, no. I just worked with him a couple of weeks ago in Florida and we had a little row with each other but he was not feeling well, he was sick and he didn’t really want to be at the gig. It’s a typical thing. So we may have like five minutes of tension and then everything, oh, well, forget about it man.
